newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telmex ADRs ease in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telmex ADRs ease in New York.

text.p: Telefonos de Mexico, or Telmex, eased on Tuesday to highlight trade in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) and foreign shares.

The telephone company's ADRs fell 1/2 to 37-1/2 after Telmex reported disappointing 1996 results. Volume was heavy, with 1.7 million shares traded by late morning, and Telmex was the most active ADR in New York.
"They did not come in near consensus and the big question is predictability," a trader said. "It was a negative surprise."
Analysts said the former monopoly was still fighting a weak economy at the same time it had to fend off new rivals.

Among European shares, Swedish telecommunications group AB LM Ericsson fell 1-1/4 to 33-1/4 after it reported 1996 results slightly above expectations. The share had slipped in Stockholm from selling by traders long in the stock.
Finnish telecommunications company Nokia Group also eased, dropping 1-3/8 to 65-3/8.
Anglo-Dutch consumer products group Unilever Plc jumped 9-1/4 to 177-3/8 after it reported a 15 percent rise in annual profits and put its specialty chemicals unit up for sale.

ADRs in British news and information group Reuters Holdings Plc fell 1-5/8 to 61-5/8 after the company reported 1996 earnings and said it would be hard to improve on its underlying revenue growth rate this year.
Israel's ECI Telecom Ltd was down 1/16 to 20-13/16 after Lehman Brothers cut its quarterly earnings estimate for the company.
Decliners led advancers by 253 to 233 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 35 million shares at midday.
